# Pixel 8 Battery Health

> Free Android app (APK) that shows Pixel 8 battery health and what is draining the battery: the capacity the battery holds now compared with its 4,550 mAh design capacity, the charge cycle count, temperature, voltage, current, live power in watts averaged over 30 seconds, Android's per-app battery use since the last charge, and the battery's manufacture and first-use dates. No root needed. Distributed as an APK on GitHub, not on Google Play.

Key facts:

- Latest version: 1.1, released 2026-11-10, 3.5 MB, Android 8.0 or newer. Built and tested on a Pixel 8 with Android 17. Version 1.0 was released 2026-10-26.
- Package name: dev.rubiks.batterybuddy
- Cycle count needs Android 14 or newer and no extra setup.
- Live power is a 30-second average. Opening or switching apps spikes power for a few seconds, so the app leaves out the spike from opening it and shows the current reading and the peak next to the average. When the phone is plugged in but not charging, the reading is only the battery's share, and the app says so.
- The "Since last charge" card shows time on battery, mAh used with the screen on and off, what used it (mobile data, CPU, screen, GPU) and the top 5 apps with how much of each app's use happened while it was not on screen. It reads Android's own battery stats.
- Android's measured capacity, its health score, the battery dates and the "Since last charge" card need three permissions granted once over adb: BATTERY_STATS, DUMP and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS. Without them the app estimates health from the current charge.
- Other phones can install it; the design capacity is built in for the Pixel 8 only.
- Battery readings and per-app battery use stay on the phone. The app shows one Google AdMob banner ad.
- Source code is not published.
- Not affiliated with Google.
